US-522 REOPEN CLOSED + COMMITTED (Sprint 70 / V0.29.25, 5/8 done). *** BL-029 IS CLEARED -- commits work again. *** PM resolved it in 0f40705; the stale .git/index.lock is gone, and US-525's previously-uncommitted fileset was committed by PM as c799a0c. My work this iteration is committed as 2412227. Verify with `ls .git/index.lock` before assuming you are blocked, but expect it to be fine.

WHAT AC5 NEEDED: --password-store=basic on the eclipse-dashboard ExecStart in BOTH variants (.x11 full rationale, .wayland pointer so they cannot drift). AC1-4 were already closed in the first pass; the reopen was only the keyring half.

THE LOAD-BEARING LESSON -- A VALUED SWITCH NEEDS A VALUE ASSERTION, and it is the same trap this story already hit one layer down. The first pass learned --disable-gpu is a SUBSTRING of --disable-gpu-rasterization, so guards must TOKENIZE the ExecStart. Tokenizing is still not enough for --password-store, because it takes a VALUE: `'--password-store' in flags` passes on --password-store=gnome, which is precisely the broken config the story deletes. So the helper returns the VALUE LIST and a dedicated fence asserts it is `basic`, never gnome/gnome-libsecret/kwallet. MUTATION-PROVED on the real unit (basic->gnome turned 3 guards red, then reverted + re-verified), not only in the synthetic self-test. Carry this: for any --flag=value switch, presence is the wrong question.

SCOPE QUESTION ANSWERED BY EVIDENCE, NOT ASSUMED. The splash units launch chromium through the SAME Debian wrapper with no --password-store, so 'is a dashboard-only fix complete?' was real. The journal settled it: gcr-prompter PerformPrompt fired at Aug 03 05:43:09 / 08:33:52 / 08:52:23 -- so the popup RECURS as the AC claimed -- and EVERY one is ~9h AFTER splash-boot exited (Aug 02 20:20:21), with NONE inside the splash's own 9.806s window. The prompts track the LONG-RUNNING dashboard chromium, so AC5's scope is correct and sufficient. Root cause confirmed on the box too: Default_Keyring.keyring at 0600 (password-protected) + gnome-keyring-daemon --components=pkcs11,secrets under passwordless auto-login; and post-fix chromium logs `key_storage_linux.cc:116 Selected backend for OSCrypt: BASIC_TEXT`.

FILED TD-076 INSTEAD OF WIDENING SCOPE, and its non-obvious half is the point: 'the splash is short-lived' only holds on a HEALTHY boot. Per the A-1 contract a DEGRADED boot DELIBERATELY KEEPS THE SPLASH UP -- exactly the long-running condition that produced the dashboard's popup. So a keyring dialog can paint over the one screen the operator most needs to read. When something is safe 'because it doesn't live long', go find the branch where it does.

UNPLANNED FINDING PM/DEPLOY SHOULD KNOW -- THE LIVE UNIT IS DRIFTED FROM THE REPO. The installed /etc/systemd/system/eclipse-dashboard.service is a PRE-US-522 copy (no US-522 header) that was HAND-PATCHED with four flags on one line: --password-store=basic --disable-gpu-rasterization --enable-logging=stderr --remote-debugging-port=9222. So (a) the deploy has NOT run since US-522 landed -- independently matching US-524's finding that set-gpu-cma.sh is not on the box; (b) Atlas live-tested the keyring fix alongside the NARROWER --disable-gpu-rasterization, not the repo's --disable-gpu. The two fixes are orthogonal (OSCrypt backend vs GPU command buffer) so the keyring result stands, but the shipped combination is not literally the tested one -- which is why validationCriteria #2 says --disable-gpu* with a wildcard. (c) On the next deploy install.sh overwrites the unit, so the three hand-added debug/raster flags vanish and --disable-gpu + --password-store=basic take effect.

DELIBERATELY DID NOT ADOPT THE DEBUG FLAGS SITTING BESIDE THE FIX. --remote-debugging-port=9222 on a car-mounted kiosk is unauthenticated full-page DevTools control; --enable-logging=stderr was Atlas's aid for reading the OSCrypt line. A test now FENCES --remote-debugging-* so it cannot arrive later by copy-paste from the box. Trade-off stated honestly: without --enable-logging the OSCrypt line will NOT be in the journal on the deployed unit, which is why the drill reads `pgrep -a chromium` plus absence of a gcr-prompter process rather than grepping for a log line.

GATE, SYNCHRONOUS, IN-LOOP: RED first (2 of 5 new guards failed for the right reason -- missing flag); then test_dashboard_kit.py 59 passed and the FULL tests/deploy 410 passed with ZERO SKIPS (both shipped templates changed, so the whole deploy contract ran; skip count read on purpose per US-524). ruff clean on the one touched .py. PRE-EXISTING RED, NOT MINE: TD-073 promise-tag lint = US-529 in this sprint. TD-075 still stands so lint is per-touched-file; `make` is NOT on PATH (make lint exits 127, which reads like a pass).

OWED, NOT FAKED: validationCriteria #2 needs a PM deploy (handbook 13). After it, `pgrep -a chromium` should show BOTH --disable-gpu AND --password-store=basic with no gcr-prompter process. It cannot be claimed from here -- the box is still running the hand-patched pre-US-522 unit.

NEXT UP is US-526 (production drain-event writer, M, the BL-028 carry-over). Its traps are already spelled out in the AC: read the UPS LATE-BOUND at transition time (the boot-order trap, now five sightings across US-501/502/503/505), and the boot reaper MUST NOT call endDrainEvent -- it derives runtime_seconds from a timestamp delta, so across a reboot it would manufacture a multi-hour runtime. The reaper stamps end_timestamp ONLY, leaving runtime_seconds AND end_vcell_v NULL. US-527 rides with it (Spool [EXACT] depth-gate values, 429a3ed) -- do not land the band-remap without the writer.
